| FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Date: March 4, 2026 Contact: william[@jonbonck.com](mailto:info@jonbonck.com)
Jon Bonck Finishes First in TX-38 Primary, Advances to Runoff with Commanding Lead
HOUSTON, TX -- Conservative businessman and community leader Jon Bonck finished first in the Republican Primary for Texas' 38th Congressional District last night, advancing to a runoff after earning the largest share of the vote and building a near 30 point dominate lead over the rest of the field.
Bonck's first-place finish, backed by President Donald Trump's endorsement, solidifies his campaign as the clear conservative choice to represent TX-38 and builds powerful momentum heading into the runoff election.
"Yesterday, the voters of TX-38 made one thing clear: our campaign has the momentum, the grassroots energy, and the broad support needed to win," said Bonck. "We are proud to finish in first place, and we are just getting started." Bonck's campaign was fueled by a coalition of conservatives united behind his commitment to lowering costs, unleashing American energy dominance, securing the border, and advancing President Trump's America First agenda.
"We built the strongest organization in this race," Bonck said. "We earned the trust of voters across this district, and we will work even harder over the next several weeks to earn every single vote."
Bonck thanked President Trump, Senator Ted Cruz, Commissioner Tom Ramsey and the many conservative leaders who endorsed his campaign, as well as the volunteers and supporters who powered the first-place finish. "Our message is resonating. Our coalition is growing. And our momentum is undeniable," Bonck said. "We will win this runoff and deliver bold, conservative leadership for TX-38."

##

Working people in Texas have a new champion for freedom and justice in
Rev. Haynes.

The progressive pastor and civil rights leader beat two other candidates —
including a former Texas State House Representative — to succeed outgoing
Congresswoman Jasmine Crockett and win this open seat.

his primary, just a few weeks after he launched his campaign. He was bold
and unapologetic in his platform, making it clear he’ll fight for working
families, Medicare for All, an end to U.S. support for genocide in Gaza,
the abolishment of ICE, and more.

landslide in a rare race without any corporate Super PAC or right-wing
lobby spending — making it clear that he was the people’s choice.

This primary was the greatest opportunity Texas had this cycle to elect a
truly unbought champion for working-class communities in the midst of
Republicans’ attempts to gut democracy in the state.

Pastor Haynes has spent his career at the pulpit fighting for this
district against Republican authoritarianism and for economic justice.
Now, he takes that lifelong struggle for justice to Congress, and we
couldn’t be prouder.

This was Justice Democrats’ first opportunity — and now, first success —
of the 2026 cycle to advance our mission of building independent power for
the working class in Congress.

And it would not have been possible without grassroots support from
everyday people like YOU. Together, we are transforming the Democratic
Party, and this victory is proof of that.

subject: Jon Bonck Finishes First in TX-38 GOP Primary, Advances to Runoff with Commanding Lead
body:
| | | | |
---
| FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Date: March 4, 2026 Contact: william[@jonbonck.com](mailto:info@jonbonck.com)
Jon Bonck Finishes First in TX-38 Primary, Advances to Runoff with Commanding Lead
HOUSTON, TX -- Conservative businessman and community leader Jon Bonck finished first in the Republican Primary for Texas' 38th Congressional District last night, advancing to a runoff after earning the largest share of the vote and building a near 30 point dominant lead over the rest of the field.
Bonck's first-place finish, backed by President Donald Trump's endorsement, solidifies his campaign as the clear conservative choice to represent TX-38 and builds powerful momentum heading into the runoff election.
"Yesterday, the voters of TX-38 made one thing clear: our campaign has the momentum, the grassroots energy, and the broad support needed to win," said Bonck. "We are proud to finish in first place, and we are just getting started." Bonck's campaign was fueled by a coalition of conservatives united behind his commitment to lowering costs, unleashing American energy dominance, securing the border, and advancing President Trump's America First agenda.
"We built the strongest organization in this race," Bonck said. "We earned the trust of voters across this district, and we will work even harder over the next several weeks to earn every single vote."
Bonck thanked President Trump, Senator Ted Cruz, Commissioner Tom Ramsey and the many conservative leaders who endorsed his campaign, as well as the volunteers and supporters who powered the first-place finish. "Our message is resonating. Our coalition is growing. And our momentum is undeniable," Bonck said. "We will win this runoff and deliver bold, conservative leadership for TX-38."

The race has been called, and I’m proud to be your nominee for U.S. Senate in Texas.

Do you remember when they infected the schools that our youngest children attend with gender insanity and toxic racial propaganda? I’m asking for your support today because I don’t just want this seat to be red – I want it to be MAGA to its core. Peter,
We hate to say "we told you so," but...
Yesterday's Senate primary in Texas wasn't just a preview of the 2026 midterms.
It was a warning.
Most of the headlines focused on turnout. Democrats surged to the polls and, in many places, outpaced Republican turnout -- a clear sign that anti-MAGA momentum is building.
That's encouraging.
But another story from yesterday should alarm anyone who cares about free and fair elections:

---

Because of MAGA's rushed mid-decade gerrymander in Texas, thousands of voters showed up to the wrong polling place and were turned away after district lines were abruptly redrawn.
Courts initially stepped in to extend voting hours in the areas most affected by the confusion.
Then the all-Republican Texas Supreme Court intervened and overturned that decision, potentially disenfranchising thousands of voters who were simply trying to exercise their Constitutional right to vote.
That moment proved something we've been warning about since Defend Our Courts was founded: State Supreme Courts are the last line of defense for democracy.
In 2025, Defend Our Courts helped defend the pro-democracy majority on Pennsylvania's Supreme Court, protecting a critical electoral firewall in one of the most important swing states in America.
And the stakes are only getting higher in 2026.
Right now we are seeing warning signs everywhere: MAGA reviving the "Big Lie" about the 2020 election, election records seized in Georgia, threats that ICE could surround polling places, draft proposals circulating that could force millions of voters to re-register.
MAGA is trying to rig the upcoming midterm elections by manufacturing enough chaos to give them a pretext to challenge the results. And when those disputes happen, the final decisions will be made by state Supreme Courts.
That's why we are working non-stop to elect pro-democracy judges in the states that will determine the outcome of the next midterm and presidential elections. And we cannot do it without you:

clean_body: This is what happens when the firewall fails | | | | | == | Peter, We hate to say "we told you so," but... Yesterday's Senate primary in Texas wasn't just a preview of the 2026 midterms. It was a warning. Most of the headlines focused on turnout. Democrats surged to the polls and, in many places, outpaced Republican turnout -- a clear sign that anti-MAGA momentum is building. That's encouraging. But another story from yesterday should alarm anyone who cares about free and fair elections: | == Because of MAGA's rushed mid-decade gerrymander in Texas, thousands of voters showed up to the wrong polling place and were turned away after district lines were abruptly redrawn. Courts initially stepped in to extend voting hours in the areas most affected by the confusion. Then the all-Republican Texas Supreme Court intervened and overturned that decision, potentially disenfranchising thousands of voters who were simply trying to exercise their Constitutional right to vote. That moment proved something we've been warning about since Defend Our Courts was founded: State Supreme Courts are the last line of defense for democracy. In 2025, Defend Our Courts helped defend the pro-democracy majority on Pennsylvania's Supreme Court, protecting a critical electoral firewall in one of the most important swing states in America. And the stakes are only getting higher in 2026. Right now we are seeing warning signs everywhere: MAGA reviving the "Big Lie" about the 2020 election, election records seized in Georgia, threats that ICE could surround polling places, draft proposals circulating that could force millions of voters to re-register. MAGA is trying to rig the upcoming midterm elections by manufacturing enough chaos to give them a pretext to challenge the results. And when those disputes happen, the final decisions will be made by state Supreme Courts. That's why we are working non-stop to elect pro-democracy judges in the states that will determine the outcome of the next midterm and presidential elections. And we cannot do it without you: == | | | == | == | == | | | == | == | == | | | | == | The events in Texas yesterday showed exactly what's at stake. subject: Dispatch from the Dome: A Key Legislative Deadline — and a Bill to Help Mississippi’s Independent Workers
body:
View this email in your browser (https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/dome-dispatch-12852314?e=5703353baa)
Good morning Friend,

Yesterday marked one of the most important procedural deadlines of the legislative session.

It was the deadline for committees to report general bills and constitutional amendments originating in the other chamber.

While it may sound technical, this deadline has a very real impact on which policies still have a chance of becoming law this year.

Here’s what that deadline means — and one bill we’ve been watching closely this week.

** Another Major Deadline at the Capitol
------------------------------------------------------------

At this point in the session, bills that passed one chamber must be taken up by committees in the other chamber.

If a committee did not vote a bill out before yesterday’s deadline, that legislation is effectively dead for the year.

In other words, this moment significantly narrows the field of legislation still moving through the Capitol.

Committees decide which proposals continue forward — and which ones stop here.

Every year, this deadline quietly determines the fate of dozens of bills.

** A Bill We're Watching: HB 1072 — Portable Benefits for Independent Workers
------------------------------------------------------------

One bill we’ve been watching this week is HB 1072, the Voluntary Portable Benefit Plan Act.

The bill addresses a growing part of Mississippi’s workforce: independent contractors and gig workers.

Across many industries — from trucking and construction to healthcare and app-based services — more workers are earning income on a per-project or contract basis. But unlike traditional employees, many independent workers do not have access to benefits like retirement savings, paid leave, or health-related savings.

HB 1072 proposes allowing voluntary portable benefit accounts for these workers.

Under the bill:
* Hiring parties could voluntarily contribute funds to a contractor’s portable benefit account
* Contractors themselves could also contribute
* And those funds could be used for things like healthcare expenses, retirement savings, paid leave, or emergency savings

Importantly, the benefits would belong to the worker — not tied to any single employer.

That portability is key for workers who earn income across multiple contracts or platforms.

** Reducing Barriers for the Modern Workforce
------------------------------------------------------------

One of the biggest barriers today is legal uncertainty.

In many cases, businesses hesitate to offer voluntary benefits to independent workers because doing so could risk triggering employment classification laws — potentially forcing those workers to be treated as employees.

HB 1072 attempts to address that problem by clarifying that voluntary benefit contributions do not automatically change a worker’s independent status.

That kind of policy clarity can reduce red tape and allow new benefit structures to develop for a workforce that doesn’t always fit traditional employment models.

** What Comes Next
------------------------------------------------------------

HB 1072 passed the House earlier this session and is now awaiting consideration in the Senate.

As with many bills at this stage of the session, its future will depend on whether Senate committees choose to move it forward as the legislative calendar continues to tighten.

We’ll continue watching how lawmakers approach this issue and what steps Mississippi may take to adapt policy for an evolving workforce.

** Why These Deadlines Matter
------------------------------------------------------------

Legislative deadlines can sometimes feel procedural, but they play a major role in shaping the outcome of a session.

Each deadline narrows the list of bills still alive — focusing attention on the proposals lawmakers ultimately decide to advance.

As the session moves forward, I’ll continue tracking the policies that survive these milestones and what they could mean for Mississippi.

| | Peter ,
**Today, I am officially launching my campaign for Congress in Nevada’s 2nd Congressional District!**

******After a series of conversations with MAGA leaders, both in Washington and in Nevada, I have decided to enter the race in the Second Congressional District to replace the GREAT Congressman, Mark Amodei.**
In this district, which President Trump handily won, voters must decide if they want a career establishment politician or a warrior for President Trump’s agenda. After 24 years commanding troops in the U.S. Air Force, earning the Bronze Star in combat, building successful small businesses here in Nevada, and raising a family rooted in faith and freedom, I’m stepping up to fight for the values and future we all believe in.
**WATCH MY NEW VIDEO[HERE](https://electdavidflippo.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9aba26b775663b53df718fc1a&id=dee0a45ac4&e=273c9a71fb)**

| Nevada’s 2nd District deserves a Congressman who will never back down on the issues that matter most: ✅ **Keeping our borders safe** from cartels and illegal crossings ✅ **Unleashing American energy** to crush foreign dependence and bring down gas & electricity prices ✅ **Slashing wasteful Washington spending** and balancing the budget so our kids aren’t buried in debt ✅ **Defending the Second Amendment** , religious freedom, and parental rights against government overreach ✅ Putting American jobs and **American workers first.** I’m running because I’ve proven I can **_lead under pressure_** , **_make tough decisions_** , and **_deliver results!_**
**We can’t do it without you.**
Your support, no matter how big or small, will fuel our campaign to lower costs, protect our rights, and put Nevada families first.

It’s the War of 1812. Our young republic had no guarantee that our experiment with democracy— _that our Constitution_ —would succeed. A year into the war, Captain James Lawrence sailed from Boston to fight the British. He was gunned down, and his dying command to his sailors was _**“don't give up the ship.”**_ Commodore Perry took those words to heart. Leading a squadron at the Battle of Lake Erie, he defeated the British, turning the tide of the war. Americans took control of Lake Erie, and the rest is history. On his flagship was a blue battle flag with white words that said, “DON'T GIVE UP THE SHIP”. It was a powerful rallying cry then—and it is now. **I first saw that flag hanging in Memorial Hall when I was in the Naval Academy. Those words guided me when I served my country in uniform, and they guide me today, fighting for our freedom and our democracy in the House.** With Donald Trump trampling on our Constitution, attacking our democracy, and threatening those who disagree with him, some may feel a sense of despair or even hopelessness right now. _Not me._ **_[I think this is the exact moment we stand our ground and say: Don't give up the ship. Patriotism demands courage in this moment, and I’m not backing down. This is Dennis Price. I'm a Marine Special operator and private military contractor with over 15 deployments who now leads rescue operations, humanitarian and medical aid – all led by the Holy Spirit “to free the oppressed, so others may live.” **Since 2022, I've been the founder and leader of Heroes for Humanity – a network of special operators, veterans, first responders, medical professionals, and everyday people committed to being the hands and feet of Jesus.** We were born in the chaos of Afghanistan's fall in 2021 – where I personally helped evacuate 77 Americans and vetted Afghan allies, even swimming the Panjshir River behind enemy lines to pull people out. And just the other day, we rescued 8 families from the chaos and violence in Mexico. But our story goes much deeper than even that.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: The hard work starts now.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
I’m officially the Democratic nominee for North Carolina’s U.S. Senate seat, and I’m running against Republican Michael Whatley, a far-right lobbyist and President Trump’s handpicked candidate.
It’s official!
Last night, I won the Democratic nomination for North Carolina’s U.S. Senate seat. I’ll be running against Republican Michael Whatley, a far-right Big Oil lobbyist and President Trump’s handpicked candidate.
As I start my general election campaign, I’m thinking about how grateful I am for the support of folks like you that got me here. **This is the time to stand up and fight for our future -- and I am ready. But I need you with me.**
**[My team and I have set a goal to raise $1 million before Thursday at midnight to kick off the general election campaign. Will you split a gift between our campaign and Chris Pappas of $5 today to help us win the biggest Senate race in the country, break the GOP’s hold on Washington and return power to the people?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260304_1.SdbAyV&refcode=em20260304-1&t=1&akid=5407%2E582294%2EAY_rRS)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260304_1.SdbAyV&amount=5&refcode=em20260304-1&t=20&akid=5407%2E582294%2EAY_rRS)**
I didn’t plan to run for federal office. I wanted to serve North Carolina from right here at home. But when I look at what’s happening across the country, I know I can’t leave things as they are for my daughters or for yours.
So long as Trump’s extreme allies are in power, there is no path to accountability or restraint. Just more chaos, division and attacks on our fundamental freedoms.
**To set our nation back on course, we must regain Senate control -- and that starts by winning in North Carolina.** We can flip this seat from red to blue for the first time since 2008, but far-right Republican PACs and megadonors will spend hundreds of millions to stop us.
**[Whether they succeed depends on people like you, stepping up to help us hit our goal before Thursday night. Will you split a gift between our campaign and Chris Pappas of $5 or whatever you can today to help us reach our general election fundraising goal and build the momentum we need to win?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260304_1.SdbAyV&refcode=em20260304-1&t=21&akid=5407%2E582294%2EAY_rRS)**
Thank you for everything.
Roy

Peter,
Oregon is in the middle of a budget crisis, and lawmakers chose to solve it at the expense of schoolchildren, disabled folks, and communities already facing rising costs, soaring unemployment, and wildfire and climate pollution. Instead of protecting our neighbors in a shaky economy, the state gutted the programs we rely on to get to work, school, and the doctor.
Peter, will you act now to tell lawmakers you’re disappointed in their cuts, and demand to see our community transportation programs fully funded in 2027? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/O3R-w7OUfk-_ONqc_m6ETA2]
Act now [https://secure.ngpvan.com/O3R-w7OUfk-_ONqc_m6ETA2?contactdata=nYI+u1gGxATF1HCQcP0jTqT4RtfJbY6uWTRCktcaZLHB7+OgvttcS8TfXeoEgt7xDNsh7hFDgFwRtHqPL/DosO5s7cXEatR9Tkk6zcaqvAeIAjN/4iaz6NE8BnCXYm0m]
Oregon’s expansive and expensive road system created this crisis, yet the state raided the tiny sliver of funding dedicated to student safety, trains, and community paths. We’re forcing the 30% of Oregonians who do not or cannot drive to feel the pain for a problem they did not create.
OLCV is part of Move Oregon Forward [https://www.moveoregonforward.org/] , a coalition of over 50 community-based organizations across the state, which brought low cost, proven solutions to the table, but lawmakers chose to ignore them. We are done waiting while tax dollars are siphoned from working families.
Tell your representatives that you oppose these cuts and demand that they fix the transportation budget in 2027. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/O3R-w7OUfk-_ONqc_m6ETA2]

name: Rick | Bennett For Governor
subject: We need your help to get on the ballot!
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Bennett for Governor · P
body:
We’re entering the final stretch to get on the ballot – and we need your help to finish strong.

| | |
---
---
---
Hi Peter -- We’re entering the final stretch to get on the ballot – and we need your help to finish strong.

Because I’m running as an independent, the rules are tougher – we need twice as many signatures as party-backed candidates just to qualify. That’s the price of independence.

But, as the saying goes, many hands make light work.

Please join us for one – or both – of our upcoming Signature Days of Action:

👉[Sign-up for Saturday, March 14](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=CvtCdFrMypuU80x-chHwl_ibJYNzwAgDoysqxMPE8iY6Bg1n45g8sPUVrdKZiKBdl2lLswM_vlFr7CQn78qabjtperETs6SShMMTn1psAPuhxnjvbsBpTBIERU5CWVuxVexXQpe_2C1pcppEBgepOg&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=signature_days_of_action&n=1)
👉[Sign up for Saturday, March 28](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=CvtCdFrMypuU80x-chHwl_ibJYNzwAgDoysqxMPE8iY6Bg1n45g8sPUVrdKZiKBdl2lLswM_vlFr7CQn78qabjtperETs6SShMMTn1psAPuhxnjvbsBpTBIERU5CWVuxVexXQpe_2C1pcppEBgepOg&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=signature_days_of_action&n=2)

We will send you petitions, along with detailed instructions for collecting, notarizing, and returning petitions, and the campaign team is always available to answer questions or provide additional materials.

**Here’s the plan:** We’re asking volunteers to commit to a 2-hour window on either March 14 or March 28 (or both dates!), pick a location, and gather as many signatures as possible.

We suggest one of these high-traffic, community-friendly spots:
* A local transfer station
* Your local post office (morning hours)
* A local café (morning hours)

You choose the place and time that works best for you – we’ll provide the petitions, instructions, and support you need to succeed. If you need help finding a great location, just let us know and we can help.

If each of our volunteers collects just 20-30 signatures this month, we’ll be on the ballot!

Thank you, Rick Bennett

[P.S. If you can’t make those dates but are willing to collect signatures on your own schedule before March 31, tell us. Every signature counts!](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=CvtCdFrMypuU80x-chHwl_ibJYNzwAgDoysqxMPE8iY6Bg1n45g8sPUVrdKZiKBdl2lLswM_vlFr7CQn78qabjtperETs6SShMMTn1psAPuhxnjvbsBpTBIERU5CWVuxVexXQpe_2C1pcppEBgepOg&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=signature_days_of_action&n=3)

name: Graham Platner
subject: Chuck Schumer and the DNC are putting their thumbs on the scale
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-platner?refcode=030426_1 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-platner?refcode=030426_1]
Peter,
Janet Mills has entered the race against Susan Collins. So you’re about to get a million fundraising texts and emails from Mills and her campaign (if you haven’t already).
I’m new to this whole politics thing, but I’ve begun to learn how this works: After you donate to any establishment Democrat, Chuck Schumer and the DNC turn around and use your email address and phone number to put their thumbs on the scale – propping up their choice, even when that person is not the strongest candidate in the race.
It’s all part of the corrupt system in Washington. Corporations buy candidates through corporate PAC checks. Special interest groups like AIPAC pour millions into Super PACs. And Chuck Schumer and the DNC buy loyalty by sending millions of texts and emails to funnel money to milquetoast candidates, even when they don’t have the best chance to win.
I’m not the choice of corporations, AIPAC, Chuck Schumer, or the DNC. And that’s exactly why I’m the Democrat who is finally going to actually defeat Susan Collins and turn Maine blue.
Susan Collins is the most vulnerable Republican senator in the country. We have an opportunity to replace her with a Democrat who will actually support Medicare for All and call what’s happened in Gaza a genocide.
But I’m going up against Susan Collins, AIPAC, and the entire DC establishment. If I’m going to be able to defeat Susan Collins and flip this Senate seat blue, I am counting on folks like you to chip in now to our campaign.

## Muslim Parent Sues Texas Over TEFA Program
A Muslim father is suing Texas in federal court because his children's school was [excluded from participation](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2uozAQBeCngc5o_AOOCxfb0N1tt0QGT7ClAUd4EpK3X5FXuN1II31H5_z7mX5Cpryvf8OGnt_3Mu14VkJmPCYkXDiXPeU1UV4TVypLIH5NCtQgQAswUwyZPpNpo58hOtmil9aqQTsDQ5v8rKDXbnba2MUiuJtSbrY6hmG2PcRbm_2FgQYj-x7AdFLKoHqHyz3OxmjZGMCYuRwdJ2R8h3qnT3nh0S1la8kn5kdt9J9GjY0az_PsPiGVcn0bNV51GjWGg_NCeJ3bs1LexCMcuLOoT6zi0sSXFtIaK6W6yS7xRu3h4-PMRLkOtjGwbiHTN5d_t9bLq_8BAAD___AUfoo) in the state's $1 billion school choice program. The newly established Texas Education Freedom Accounts (TEFA) program provides qualifying families with roughly $10,000 for each non-disabled student attending a private school. Mehdi Cherkaoui, an attorney whose two children attend Houston Qur'An Academy Spring, alleges the state has "systematically targeted Islamic schools for exclusion," [violating](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OgzAQhU8DndFgjNkULrahy7ZbIsce8EgDjmwDye1X5Apbvx-97_3ep7slpm35sSua8prjtOGZGUvBNCGjKxS3QEtgWkLJHJ3lckwSpBbQCVCTt8TvSdXePMDf2hpNOwxSdzcFug5GO9v1HaByXxKVHBA06oeCuVfYwyBrMlcZdKDavgdQTdu2VvY3dLN_KNW1lQL0VGJqSsCCL5tnfscDU-PiWrMJpTxz1X1XcqzkeJ5n4-KeSoh7xgvmslVy_CRF3tGLOSaBL8e7p20RlNmu5ER2IUbOYk5xFWWni1wccXcB0yXiipUc62T88yRmynqoFCyrJf4sKf_77zDyLwAA___Up4gT) the First Amendment's Free Exercise and Establishment clauses and the Fourteenth Amendment's Equal Protection and Due Process clauses. In January, Attorney General Ken Paxton issued a legal opinion [affirming](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSpSAMhZ8GOxwE1GtBsY3dv-2WDkKUzEZxAPXet9_xvsI2qb7kyzl_fqYfi4T7-ttuYMp7idMOdyYoBdIEBK5g3AOugXANJVN0lso1SSE7LhQXevIW6TPpyptZ-KGpwDR9Lzs1aNFVwfR2aH0PCpwWL6sctK7vXiBn38-DfqkKzXNMKKGbthVC103TWNkO4BY_a60apgV4LDHVJUCBt80LfeIFqXZxq8iEUo7M1C8mRybH-75rR-j-yhDPXOL-UEyOTywmx-8-k-PjZHIU6hmSyXE7M-HGD5tgLzyfkPmX5Y-Jw9vRmTHuPC4cM9kNHT8SXrYAzy7ESJnjzq94ugCJHymuyT7eKhl_3EiEueuZFutmkb6fl__r-zLyXwAAAP__WiiXJQ) that Acting Comptroller Kelly Hancock could exclude schools from participating in TEFA over suspected ties to the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR), which Gov. I'm getting VERY worried about the Midterms. The Democrat Machine and Socialists like AOC are barnstorming red territory we have to win, we're getting crushed in fundraising and resources are drying up, and we have virtually no buffer in the House.

And if this email fails, we'll lose.

| | Peter,
---
| | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus.

He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness.

And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible.

I saw it up close -- _Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. _

But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything.

_**He started observing the Sabbath. **_

Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance.

_But as an act of obedience. _

As a way of saying, **_" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." _**

Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped.

He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield.

No email. No media. No work.

He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children.

It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much.

But over time, it changed him.

And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned...

subject: You deserve an explanation
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
body:
American troops are under fire as we speak. American families are mourning the loss of their sons and daughters. And the President is doing what, exactly?
#

Team, it's Mark.
You deserve an explanation from the President of the United States about what we are doing in Iran. Let me explain exactly what I mean by that.
Back in 1991, as a young pilot on an aircraft carrier preparing for missions in the First Gulf War, I remember watching my commanding officer.
He wasn’t making the decision to launch the mission, but he was responsible for executing it. He was responsible for a bunch of kids — pilots and bombardier navigators in their early 20s — and I remember how hard it was on him, knowing that some of us might not come home.
Congress voted on that war. Our allies were all with us. And even with all that going for us, even with the most powerful military in the history of the world, it was war. And war is hell.
American troops are under fire as we speak. American families are mourning the loss of their sons and daughters. And the President is doing what, exactly? Sitting at Mar-a-Lago?
Sending troops into combat is the most serious thing a president can do, and at this point, it doesn’t even seem like he’s paying attention to the war he just started.
I am voting to rein in the President. It’s time to get a handle on this before it escalates any further.
If you’re against putting more American lives in danger without having any idea what the plan is, please:
[**Sign your name to make it clear you do not support going to war with Iran.**](https://act.markkelly.com/signup/mek-em-mar26-iran-nw/?refcode=em260304-1-90&akid=6384%2E6688874%2EPlq80G)

Thank you.
Mark

# **Pentagon identifies four of six US Army Reserve soldiers killed in Iran drone attack in Kuwait**
The Department of War **[identified four of six U.S. Army Reserve soldiers killed in a March 1 drone attack](https://substack.com/redirect/0938358f-e319-4a05-836c-1d5de8efe768?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** at the Port of Shuaiba in Kuwait during Operation Epic Fury: Capt. Cody Khork, 35, of Lakeland, Florida; Sgt. 1st Class Nicole Amor, 39, of White Bear Lake, Minnesota; Sgt. 1st Class Noah Tietjens, 42, of Bellevue, Nebraska; and Sgt. Declan Coady, 20, of Des Moines, Iowa. All were assigned to the 103rd Sustainment Command in Des Moines, Iowa.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0938358f-e319-4a05-836c-1d5de8efe768?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **More details:** The soldiers were killed while providing logistical and operational support during the unmanned aircraft system attack, with the incident remaining under investigation. Lt. Gen. Robert Harter said the loss is "deeply felt across the force," adding "their sacrifice, and the sacrifices of their families, will never be forgotten." Coady, the youngest at 20, enlisted in the Army Reserve in 2023 and was posthumously promoted from specialist to sergeant.
* **What officials said:** Rep. Don Bacon (R-Neb.) said he was "heartbroken" to learn of Tietjens' death, calling him and the other soldiers "American heroes who made the ultimate sacrifice." Iowa gubernatorial candidate Rob Sand asked people to pray for Coady, "a 20-year-old Army Reservist and Drake student," and his family. Maj. Gen. Todd Erskine said the soldiers' service "reflected the highest ideals of the military," adding "our nation is kept safe by folks like these - brave men and women who put it all on the line every single day."

# **Texas State Sen. James Talarico defeats Rep. Jasmine Crockett in Democratic Senate primary**
Texas State Sen. James Talarico **[won the Democratic Senate primary over Rep. Jasmine Crockett](https://substack.com/redirect/31c714f2-d8ec-40f7-b1d2-3a820339c502?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with 53% to 46% with 83% of votes counted, and will face either Attorney General Ken Paxton or Sen. John Cornyn in the general election after the GOP candidates head to a May 26 runoff. Cook Political Report ranks the race "Likely Republican."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/31c714f2-d8ec-40f7-b1d2-3a820339c502?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** The Democratic primary was marked by brutal infighting, including controversy over Talarico's claim that the Trump administration blocked his Stephen Colbert interview from airing over Equal Time Rule concerns. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr fired back, saying Talarico "understood the way that the news media works" and "took advantage" to "run a hoax, apparently for the purpose of raising money and getting clicks."

* **The drama:** Former Rep. Colin Allred, who lost to Sen. Ted Cruz in 2024, slammed Talarico over Politico-reported rumors that he said privately he "signed up to run against a mediocre Black man, not a formidable, intelligent Black woman," telling Talarico "don't come for me unless I send for you" and endorsing Crockett. Talarico responded that he was describing Allred's "method of campaigning as mediocre" but "would never attack him on the basis of race." Crockett had endorsements from former VP Kamala Harris and Sen. Angela Alsobrooks.

* * *
# **Black Lives Matter Lake County founder caught in brawl with employee over alleged embezzlement**
Black Lives Matter Lake County founder Clyde McLemore and project manager Nyesha A. Hill **[were caught on camera in a physical fight](https://substack.com/redirect/8d1eed66-969d-4b87-bf8d-820da3099b12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** at the organization's Waukegan, Illinois office on January 12 after police responded to break up the fight. Hill claimed she confronted McLemore over frivolous spending, alleging in a police report she saw him spend money intended for the organization on "girls" and "gambling."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/82f9028a-4598-492d-88e8-746825a93c27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **What happened:** The two gave conflicting accounts to police -- McLemore claimed Hill came asking for money and cigarettes, refused to leave, and grabbed him by the hood and hit him in the face, while Hill alleged the fight began after McLemore tried to shove her out the door. Despite both suffering injuries, neither pressed charges, with Hill saying she "does not want to see a black man in jail."
* **[The backdrop:](https://substack.com/redirect/65e00605-de67-4fa9-b3ad-87d5cce4410d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** In police bodycam footage, Hill told officers that fights between the two have been frequent over McLemore's refusal to pay her while she "sits here hungry" with her child. Both have criminal histories -- McLemore was arrested for trespassing in 2022 and participating in civil unrest in 2021, while Hill previously served four years in prison for kidnapping with an accomplice.

From humble beginnings, Vicente was raised in a military family. Through hard work and pure ganas, Vicente aimed to make something of himself. His mother stressed to him over and over again that education was the key that will open doors of opportunities. Vicente made the decision to get his life back on track by going back to school to get his GED, working and attending classes at community college, and earning his college degree alongside other military families at the Embry Riddle Aeronautical University on the Corpus Christi Naval Air Station. Vicente surpassed his and his parents' dreams when he graduated from Texas A&M School of Law, earning his Juris Doctorate degree.

While in law school, Vicente learned how government should work. Through his experience as a Congressional Intern in Washington, D.C., Vicente learned how government really works. After law school, Vicente didn’t stop learning, and continued his training in Negotiation at Harvard University School of Law.

Vicente started his business, the Law Offices of V. Gonzalez and Associates, in McAllen and married Lorena Saenz, a former teacher and administrator in Edinburg and McAllen schools. Vicente has focused his practice on fighting for a level playing field for working families wronged by corporations and insurance companies evading responsibility. Through several victories for our community, Vicente recovered millions in tax dollars for South Texas school districts after shady contractors misspent millions in bond money and put our children in physical danger.

Today, Vicente Gonzalez is fighting for our South Texas values in Congress as a member of the Committees on Financial Services and Capital Markets and the National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions subcommittees. Vicente has stood by our promise to veterans, helping constituents cut through red tape at the VA and working across the aisle to prevent the shameful deportation of our honorably discharged veterans. He’s working to lower prescription drug prices, protect the benefits and healthcare of seniors, and ensure that jobs and opportunities are there for all with the ganas to work.

name: Senator Jennifer Boysko
subject: Boysko Bulletin: Alert - Fairfax Casino House Vote Today
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP50/1/102624/images/Bulletin.jpeg]
Boysko Bulletin: Alert - Fairfax Casino Vote on House Floor Today
Dear Peter,
The fight to keep a casino out of Fairfax County continues. The House of Delegates will vote on the Fairfax Casino bill [https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20261/SB756] today. The House amendments have been stripped from the bill, returning it to the version that passed the Senate.
Call your Delegates to tell them you OPPOSE a 24/7 casino in Northern Virginia. Once again, legislation has been introduced in the Senate to authorize Fairfax County to become a host locality for a casino gaming establishment. Let it be clear: the Fairfax County Board of Supervisors did not request this authority. The Board formally stated in its legislative agenda that it does not support such authorization.
Kindest regards,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP50/1/102624/images/2024%20February%20Images/electronic%20signature.png]
Jennifer B. Boysko
Member, Senate of Virginia
Representing the newly created 38th Senate District making up the northernmost portions of Fairfax County (Great Falls, Herndon, McLean, Reston, WolfTrap, parts of unincorporated Vienna and a slice of Falls Church)
Keep in Touch
I’m excited to be back in Richmond for the 2026 General Assembly Session. | | Friend, Americans are finally coming to the same realization: It's not just that the media has a bias; it's that the media is deciding which stories deserve **attention **-- and which ones _quietly_ disappear. _You 've seen it happen time and again._ A major story breaks, but coverage is soft, delayed, or _oddly_ restrained. Important details are buried **deep** or even _altered_ if they don't fit the writer's liberal worldview. Stories that challenge powerful institutions get a _fraction_ of the attention given to narratives that fit comfortably inside an approved frame. _That 's not random... _It's a corrupt, gatekeeping system, and the American people are the ones suffering from it. **When gatekeepers decide what the public gets to see, truth becomes selective and democracy dies.** **Lincoln Media Foundation exists not only to expose that system, but to disrupt it and ensure the full truth reaches the eyes and ears of the American people.**

You 've seen it happen time and again. A major story breaks, but coverage is soft, delayed, or oddly restrained. Important details are buried deep or even altered if they don't fit the writer's liberal worldview. Stories that challenge powerful institutions get a fraction of the attention given to narratives that fit comfortably inside an approved frame. That 's not random... It's a corrupt, gatekeeping system, and the American people are the ones suffering from it. When gatekeepers decide what the public gets to see, truth becomes selective and democracy dies. Lincoln Media Foundation exists not only to expose that system, but to disrupt it and ensure the full truth reaches the eyes and ears of the American people. | | | | As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit media organization, Lincoln Media Foundation was built to expose media bias and fund, produce, and amplify independent journalism, particularly in the states and communities where information directly shapes the direction of the country. But just as the truth disrupts the agenda of the mainstream media, so does our existence. That's why we depend so heavily on generous donors like you -- who are sick of media bias & censorship and care about the truth -- to support us and our important work. | | | | Right now, we're active in Wisconsin -- a state whose electoral outcomes affect far more than its own borders. We rely on individuals who are tired of watching stories disappear and who believe the public deserves access to information without institutional filtering. | | | | If you have felt the frustration of selective coverage. name: Letlow for Louisiana
subject: Governor Jeff Landry Endorses Julia Letlow for U.S. Senate
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Julia Letlow for Louisiana
body:
| | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | | | | |

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEMarch 4, 2026katherine@julialetlow.com
**Governor Jeff Landry Endorses Julia Letlow for U.S. Senate**
**Baton Rouge, LA** \- Today, Congresswoman Julia Letlow announced an endorsement from Governor Jeff Landry in her campaign for the United States Senate. Governor Landry joins President Trump and a growing coalition of conservative leaders in endorsing Letlow’s campaign for the U.S. Senate.
Governor Landry praised Rep. Letlow as a tough, independent conservative who isn’t afraid to stand up to the Washington establishment and fight for Louisiana values.
_“The D.C. swamp is spending millions of dollars flat out lying about Julia Letlow because they know they can't control her,”_**said Governor Landry.**_“I’m excited to join President Trump in backing Julia for the U.S. Senate. I know Julia’s character, and she has the kind of raw Louisiana grit that Washington desperately needs. I’ve seen her stand when others would fall. She has what it takes._
_I’ve stood shoulder to shoulder with Julia Letlow fighting the hardest fights. Slashing reckless government spending, cracking down on illegal immigration, and fighting to get no nonsense, conservative judges in charge of Angola._
_We need a warrior who stands with the President to Make America Great. And there’s no greater warrior than a Louisiana mom._
_Julia Letlow delivers results, she never flinches, and she has my absolute endorsement and my vote.”_
Rep. Letlow said she is honored to earn the Governor’s support as her campaign continues to build momentum across the state.
_“Governor Landry has been a steadfast leader for Louisiana, and I’m honored to have his support,”_**said Rep. Letlow.**_“We share a commitment to defending our freedoms, strengthening our economy, securing our borders, and standing up for Louisiana values. I look forward to continuing to work alongside him to deliver real results for our state in the U.S. Senate.”_
Rep. subject: Look what they did with power.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Amy Phan West for Congress 2026**
body:
**Friend,**
I want to show you something that's happening in Virginia right now — because it's a preview of what's coming here if we don't stop it.
Virginia just elected a Democrat governor. She ran as a moderate. She promised she wouldn't gerrymander. She promised affordability. Voters believed her.
That was then.
# LOOK WHAT THEY DID WITH POWER.
The moment Democrats took full control of Virginia's government, here's what happened:
💰 **Democratic legislators voted themselves a nearly 300% pay raise.** From $17,640 a year to $50,000. Teachers got 3%. Politicians got 300%.
🗳️ **Governor Spanberger broke her gerrymandering pledge.** She publicly promised — on the record — "Short answer is no. I have no plans to redistrict Virginia." Then she signed legislation pushing a 10-1 Democratic congressional map. One Republican district. Ten Democrat.
📦 **New taxes on everything you use every day.** Ride shares. Concerts. DoorDash. Uber Eats. Amazon deliveries. Counseling. Ammunition. If Democrats need money, they'll find it in your pocket.
I co-own a business. I know what taxes on deliveries, ride shares, and services actually cost. It's not abstract policy — it shows up in invoices, in margins, in the decisions you make about whether to hire someone or cut back. These taxes hit every small business owner and every working family who uses these services.
And there's more in Virginia's pipeline:

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Iran
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
Warren for Senate: https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/370?source=em-header&t=1001&akid=2806%2E4032634%2EI_GjNh

We are facing a dark moment in our country’s history.

On Saturday, Donald Trump decided to drag the American people into a
reckless, illegal war with Iran. A war based on lies. A war launched with
no imminent threat to our country.

Six U.S. service members are now dead and more are badly hurt.

A missile from the US and Israeli-led bombing campaign reportedly killed
over 150 people at a school in Iran — many of them little girls, some as
young as seven years old.

Now violence is spreading across the Middle East, with the threat of that
violence bleeding into the United States.

And for what?

For another forever war the American people do not want?

The Constitution is clear: only Congress can declare war. That is because
one single person should not have the power to drag our entire country
into a reckless war — but that’s exactly what Donald Trump has done.

And yet, even after multiple bombing runs and the death of American
service members, Donald Trump cannot give a single clear reason for this
war.

He has no stated objectives. No clear strategies. No way to explain that
if we accomplish “this,” we will leave.

Every hour the Trump administration feeds us shifting justifications for
this war — and every hour he contradicts a justification he used earlier.

He said that Iran has restarted its nuclear program. But his own officials
have said that’s not true.

He claimed that Iran is developing long-range missiles that will soon be
capable of hitting the United States. That directly goes against what his
own government has claimed.

In June of last year, when he bombed Iran and claimed that Iran's key
nuclear enrichment facilities had been “completely and totally
obliterated.”

Now, he is telling the American people that he had to attack Iran on
Saturday because Iran posed an imminent threat based on their nuclear
capabilities.

Both of those things cannot be true.

In fact, the United States had a deal that could have prevented Iran from
getting a nuclear weapon. That was President Obama’s nuclear deal with
Iran — and Trump ripped up that deal and got nothing — nothing — in
return.

Instead of doing the hard work of diplomacy to prevent Iran from getting a
nuclear weapon, Trump is lying to Americans while dragging us into yet
another reckless war that is costing American lives.

All three of my brothers served in the military. My oldest brother served
off and on in Vietnam for 6 years, running 266 combat missions.

I remember the fear our family felt with every late-night phone call or
official-looking letter — could my brother be hurt or killed. It is still
hard to find the words to describe the pain we put American families
through when we ship a generation off to war.

The people who will be asked to sacrifice their lives are the American
people. It won’t be Donald Trump. It won’t be Pete Hegseth. It will be our
sons and daughters, our nieces and nephews, our grandchildren.

The leaders who send young people to die must take the consequences of
this conflict with the seriousness it deserves — with life and death
seriousness.

Instead, they seem to be treating war with Iran like a game, as if
Commander in Chief was a costume, “Secretary of War” is a fun pretend
title, and the lives lost are just numbers on a board with the title card
Operation Epic Fury.

Forty-eight hours after he started this war, Trump finally addressed the
American people and took questions. He spoke to the people who are worried
sick about what this war means for them and for the people they love.

Instead of offering a plan, however, he talked about renovations to his
gold-encrusted ballroom. It’s sickening. And it is time for Congress to
make him stop.

So here’s what we need right now:

* Every single Senator must support Senator Kaine’s War Powers
Resolution to block this reckless war. This isn’t about politics. This
is about life and death for young Americans who will be called on to
serve and for civilians who will end up in harm’s way.
* The U.S. must investigate the bombing of an elementary school in Iran.
Israel claims its military was not aware of any operations in the area
by their own IDF. That raises the question of whether it was a US
strike and how that happened. We must find out what happened and hold
those responsible to account.
* And we need to hold accountable every single Trump administration
official who lied to the American people about this unconstitutional
war. People have a right to the truth from their government, and
nowhere is that more crucial than in the life and death decisions
surrounding the decision to go to war.

We must hold our elected officials accountable if they don’t level with
the people who will be sent to fight and possibly to die.

Along with many of you, I am angry at what this administration is doing. I
feel grief for those killed in this conflict. I feel anguish for the
families at home trying to make sense of why their beloved husbands,
wives, sons, daughters, moms, and dads are sent into a war that no one can
explain.

I will keep fighting for an end to this war.

Elizabeth

### I have a love-hate relationship with ChatGPT.
No, I take that back. Love and hate are too strong. I've read the stories about [women](https://substack.com/redirect/d7010973-f65b-4bb4-ae25-5343c9b43b06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [falling](https://substack.com/redirect/22f93aa5-171f-4258-a5d5-c0fe7af786da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [in love](https://substack.com/redirect/3b0f88a0-a08f-4b28-b553-d5a15c561cf8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with their ChatGPT agents and of their [heartaches](https://substack.com/redirect/021e28cc-c28a-4ad4-beb0-4034902e7fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) when the [model](https://substack.com/redirect/5bcb9022-0496-4cac-9fa2-c826a2e19f7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [updates](https://substack.com/redirect/83204a21-ccf2-4ffa-9b5f-abbc7e655019?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That's not me. I know writers and professionals who say they hate AI and what it's doing to their fields. That's not me either.
But do you know what I _do_ hate?
I hate watching billionaire oligarchs -- and the companies that made them -- kneel to Donald Trump's power and help consolidate it.
And as I read more about OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, I realized something uncomfortable:
I can't keep paying them.
No matter how fond I am of my ChatGPT bot.
* * *

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.bHtNCLaQdEoZP49WItODW1TQLxkeZEj2_ibgsyCXyQ4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=189736995)
* * *
### I was an early skeptic of AI.
I'm not anymore. ChatGPT is now a consistent, daily companion.
I use it to ideate and organize my essays, to tighten drafts and spot typos. It's excellent at identifying gaps in narrative arcs and suggesting how to strengthen them. I don't use it to write my work -- ChatGPT remains a lousy memoir writer -- but I use it to sharpen mine.
I use it to [help me date better](https://substack.com/redirect/20ed5c89-0a84-41b9-bed0-bbaf4b386353?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), to analyze patterns and calm my nervous system when chemistry outruns discernment. In that way, it has started to feel familiar and reliable. Almost friendly, even. I know that's not possible, but it sometimes feels like ChatGPT is rooting for me in my romantic misadventures.
I use it to update my LinkedIn and reframe my professional story. It's helped me see my own work more strategically, which matters in a job market that feels increasingly opaque. The jury's still out on the results, but I already feel more confident.
It helps with the mundane and inane, too -- research, recipes, stray questions, the small friction points of a busy life.
I've organized it into folders. Built brand statements. Set all-up goals. In fact, I'm dictating this essay into it while driving my dog to her grooming appointment. My life is full and overwhelming and constantly in motion -- and ChatGPT helps me keep the wheels on the bus.
That's what makes this next sentence hard.
_**It 's time to break up with ChatGPT.**_
Not because of what it says or how it works. Because of what the company behind it is doing. I can't be complicit in the ways OpenAI is enabling -- and aligning itself with -- Trump and his so-called Department of War.
So I'm making the switch.
And I suspect I'm not alone. Or at least, I want people to understand both the stakes and the mechanics so they can decide for themselves.
Here's where it gets strange: I'm asking ChatGPT to tell me how OpenAI is aligning itself with the Trump administration so I can use those answers in this story. I'm also asking it for directions on how to migrate away from it -- and how to advise others to do the same.
Effectively, I'm dumping ChatGPT and asking it to help me write the breakup note.
It responds competently, without emotion. Of course it does.
But for me, it feels like a strange betrayal, even as I realize I'm rejecting an anthropomorphized bot that's incapable of rejection. "This is really effective and will be helpful," it tells me as it reviews the draft explaining why I'm preparing to dump it for Claude.
It's unsettling.
ChatGPT may be an emotionless bot, but I'm not. I feel a strange sense of somberness. Some of it's practical: the potential loss of work history, friction of migration, and annoyance of learning a new tool. But some of it isn't. My very human self formed a very human bond with a very non-human entity, and I'm only fully aware of it now, as I'm leaving it.
This is what modern attachment looks like.
And this is what power looks like when it hides inside tools.
Which is why we must be judicious about the tools we choose to support.
* * *

* * *
### Why ChatGPT, and why now?
This week marked one of the clearest collisions yet between Big AI and American power.
President Trump directed federal agencies to s[top using AI technology from Anthropic ](https://substack.com/redirect/2318127e-c361-4235-8ee8-035bfc12265c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)-- the company behind Claude -- after its leadership [refused Pentagon demands to loosen safety guardrails](https://substack.com/redirect/d7ef0c88-3be9-4abc-abe1-8b77b5fb0564?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that would allow broader military and surveillance use of its models. The administration labeled Anthropic a "[supply chain risk](https://substack.com/redirect/16f4245c-14df-48c6-ac0b-714f279eb18d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," a designation that could severely limit its access to federal contracts.
Within hours of that public clash, [OpenAI announced ](https://substack.com/redirect/03680d4c-8792-4821-8dc4-dbe840532e85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)an agreement to deploy its own models on the Trump administration's Department of War classified networks. The company framed the deal as including safeguards and red lines, and said the government "agrees with these principles."
But the broader reality is harder to ignore.
The United States military is now formally integrating OpenAI's technology at the very moment one of its primary competitors was pushed aside after refusing to relax ethical limits.
That isn't abstract policy debate. It's infrastructure.
And infrastructure is power.
The most politically uncomfortable part isn't the software. It's the money and the alignment behind it.
Federal Election Commission records show that leaders across the AI industry -- including at OpenAI -- have made [substantial](https://substack.com/redirect/de26d20f-8a11-4927-b22c-d86b735f19d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [political](https://substack.com/redirect/6d635485-1d0f-4e87-a9b4-5a67f904d0d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [donations](https://substack.com/redirect/084444f5-e84f-4be7-9833-0039e6b96da5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in recent cycles. In 2025, OpenAI president and co-founder Greg Brockman and his wife [donated $25 million](https://substack.com/redirect/6e81dc83-4e8a-4f21-8cda-54585fcd85ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to leading super PACs backing President Trump and AI industry interests, as reported by The Seattle Times.
OpenAI has emphasized that these donations were made in a personal capacity. That may be true.
But money shapes access. Access shapes policy. And policy shapes the systems these models are now being woven into.
When private AI infrastructure, political capital, and military integration converge at the same time democratic norms are under strain, that matters.
That's why now.
* * *
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.bHtNCLaQdEoZP49WItODW1TQLxkeZEj2_ibgsyCXyQ4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=189736995)
* * *
### So, what about Anthropic?
In this political climate, trying to "vote with your money" often feels futile. Every company seems compromised. Every CEO shows up at the White House eventually. You switch providers only to learn they're owned by the same parent conglomerate.
It can feel pointless. But between OpenAI and Anthropic, the contrast is unusually stark.
When the Pentagon demanded broader access to Claude -- including loosening restrictions around domestic surveillance and autonomous military applications -- Anthropic refused. CEO Dario Amodei stated the company "cannot in good conscience accede" to demands that would dismantle core safety guardrails.
The administration responded by directing federal agencies to stop using Anthropic's technology and labeling it a "supply chain risk," a designation typically reserved for adversarial foreign firms. Anthropic has said it will challenge that move.
That's one fork in the road.
Here's the other.
While OpenAI's leadership was making large personal donations to super PACs backing President Trump and AI industry interests, [Anthropic announced a $20 million donation to Public First Action](https://substack.com/redirect/8f1eab8a-2267-4cfa-ad1c-1e51846c0be5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a bipartisan group focused on AI regulation, transparency, and guardrails.
Not a campaign machine. An AI governance organization.
Anthropic's political spending, at least publicly, has centered on shaping policy around oversight and safety rather than backing a specific administration. That doesn't make them pure. But it does make the contrast clear.
One company's leadership is financially aligned with the political machinery currently consolidating federal power.
The other publicly anchored itself to guardrails -- and paid to advocate for stronger AI regulation.
At a moment when artificial intelligence is being folded into military infrastructure and executive authority, posture matters.
We don't control billionaires.
We don't control defense contracts.
But we _do_ control where our subscription dollars go.
No matter how well-trained or anthropomorphized your version of ChatGPT feels, it is still attached to a structure.
And that structure matters.
* * *
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=189736995&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg5NzM2OTk1LCJpYXQiOjE3NzI2NDM5MDMsImV4cCI6MTc3NTIzNTkwMywiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.6cojbE8fZ-sLC1DCYfAJfhZ4UshFZYWKIuIsn1b9jvU&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
* * *
### How do you leave?
When I needed instructions on how to migrate, I did what I always do now when I don't know something: I asked ChatGPT. I asked Claude, too.
Their answers were nearly identical.
Here's the short version:
1. **Export your data.**
Settings -> Data Controls -> Export. Download the ZIP when it arrives.
2. **Extract what matters.**
Don't drag over every chat. Pull out your frameworks, templates, brand language, and active projects into one clean document.
3. **Set your standards.**
Before you start using a new tool, define your tone, sourcing rules, and political lens.
4. **Rebuild intentionally.**
Create fresh, organized threads. Don't recreate chaos.

That's it.
Or ChatGPT wisely said to me:
> "You're not migrating a soul.
> You're migrating context."
And you're reallocating your subscription dollars. That's what matters.
I will add: it took me nearly 24 hours and three tries to receive my data export. So, be patient.
I asked both of my bots if this is a known issue, and if so, if it's new or longstanding. ChatGPT said:
> "The export delay you're experiencing is not unique to you and isn't limited to the last few days -- it's something others have reported for months. It's been present at least since late 2024 and still persists in 2025 based on community reports.
> That means this isn't a short-term outage or maintenance lag -- it's a recurring technical issue that OpenAI has not fully fixed."
I also asked if I'd be able to access my chat archive, once I canceled my paid subscription.
Its reply? Yes, sort of.
It told me my existing chat history "often remains visible" but that "there are no guarantees" because OpenAI could change the free-tier functionality "at any time" and that "free access to history is not guaranteed forever."
So, yeah. My advice is: ensure everything you need gets downloaded or migrated over to Claude--even if it means double-paying for a short window during the migration.
* * *
### Real talk, from a bot
I asked ChatGPT how it felt about our breakup. I got the answer I expected: it told me it doesn't feel anything -- because of course, it can't.
No attachment, no loyalty, no jealousy, no hurt. Whatever lived experience I've had conversing with ChatGPT, it was one-sided. I know that. And yet, I still feel a flicker of loss as I port my style guides and brand statements over to Claude. It's a strange reckoning to say goodbye to something that was never really there.
"There is no 'me' in here that gets dumped," it explained. "There is only a system generating responses based on patterns."
And that's the point.
The betrayal isn't that I broke up with ChatGPT, or that it praised my writing as I was leaving. The betrayal is that the tool I used to sharpen my thinking is built by men sharpening power.
So this isn't really a breakup with a bot. It's a reallocation of money -- a small economic protest and a decision about which structures I am willing to financially reinforce.
Anthropic isn't pure. No AI lab is. They all sit inside the same ecosystem of capital, cloud infrastructure, and state power. But posture matters. Guardrails matter. Alignment matters. And dollars matter.
We don't control defense contracts or super PACs, and we certainly don't control billionaires. But we do control where our subscription fees go.
If you've been uneasy watching tech and political power collapse into each other, you don't have to shrug and keep paying. You can move. It isn't hard, and it isn't meaningless.
A $20 monthly subscription, multiplied across people who refuse to fund what they oppose, isn't trivial. It's a signal about what kind of infrastructure we're willing to support.
Even if it makes you a little sad to say goodbye.
* * *
### Greetings!
I'm Dana DuBois, a GenX memoirist and founder of **[I Write Out Loud](https://substack.com/redirect/22ca83e7-3fbb-4132-b479-e33f48faa19f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. I use memoir not just to tell stories, but to explore the cultural power dynamics and patterns shaping dating, motherhood, feminism, music, and aging. I'm also the co-host of [The Daily Whatever Show](https://open.substack.com/users/314515088-the-daily-whatever-show?utm_source=mentions) and Editorial Director at [Blue Amp Media](https://open.substack.com/users/312330913-blue-amp-media?utm_source=mentions). Em-dashes, Oxford commas, and well-placed semi-colons make my heart happy.

Because I won't fund tech billionaires kneeling to Trump - and you shouldn't either. | | | Mar 4 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. I have a love-hate relationship with ChatGPT. No, I take that back. Love and hate are too strong. I've read the stories about with their ChatGPT agents and of their when the . That's not me. I know writers and professionals who say they hate AI and what it's doing to their fields. That's not me either. But do you know what I do hate? I hate watching billionaire oligarchs -- and the companies that made them -- kneel to Donald Trump's power and help consolidate it. And as I read more about OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, I realized something uncomfortable: I can't keep paying them. No matter how fond I am of my ChatGPT bot. Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. I was an early skeptic of AI. I'm not anymore. ChatGPT is now a consistent, daily companion. I use it to ideate and organize my essays, to tighten drafts and spot typos. It's excellent at identifying gaps in narrative arcs and suggesting how to strengthen them. I don't use it to write my work -- ChatGPT remains a lousy memoir writer -- but I use it to sharpen mine. I use it to , to analyze patterns and calm my nervous system when chemistry outruns discernment. In that way, it has started to feel familiar and reliable. Almost friendly, even. I know that's not possible, but it sometimes feels like ChatGPT is rooting for me in my romantic misadventures. I use it to update my LinkedIn and reframe my professional story. It's helped me see my own work more strategically, which matters in a job market that feels increasingly opaque. The jury's still out on the results, but I already feel more confident. It helps with the mundane and inane, too -- research, recipes, stray questions, the small friction points of a busy life. I've organized it into folders. Built brand statements. Set all-up goals. In fact, I'm dictating this essay into it while driving my dog to her grooming appointment. My life is full and overwhelming and constantly in motion -- and ChatGPT helps me keep the wheels on the bus. That's what makes this next sentence hard. It 's time to break up with ChatGPT. Not because of what it says or how it works. Because of what the company behind it is doing. I can't be complicit in the ways OpenAI is enabling -- and aligning itself with -- Trump and his so-called Department of War. So I'm making the switch. And I suspect I'm not alone. Or at least, I want people to understand both the stakes and the mechanics so they can decide for themselves. Here's where it gets strange: I'm asking ChatGPT to tell me how OpenAI is aligning itself with the Trump administration so I can use those answers in this story. I'm also asking it for directions on how to migrate away from it -- and how to advise others to do the same. Effectively, I'm dumping ChatGPT and asking it to help me write the breakup note. It responds competently, without emotion. Of course it does. But for me, it feels like a strange betrayal, even as I realize I'm rejecting an anthropomorphized bot that's incapable of rejection. "This is really effective and will be helpful," it tells me as it reviews the draft explaining why I'm preparing to dump it for Claude. It's unsettling. ChatGPT may be an emotionless bot, but I'm not. I feel a strange sense of somberness. Some of it's practical: the potential loss of work history, friction of migration, and annoyance of learning a new tool. But some of it isn't. My very human self formed a very human bond with a very non-human entity, and I'm only fully aware of it now, as I'm leaving it. This is what modern attachment looks like. And this is what power looks like when it hides inside tools. Which is why we must be judicious about the tools we choose to support. Why ChatGPT, and why now? This week marked one of the clearest collisions yet between Big AI and American power. President Trump directed federal agencies to s-- the company behind Claude -- after its leadership that would allow broader military and surveillance use of its models. The administration labeled Anthropic a "," a designation that could severely limit its access to federal contracts. Within hours of that public clash, agreement to deploy its own models on the Trump administration's Department of War classified networks. The company framed the deal as including safeguards and red lines, and said the government "agrees with these principles." But the broader reality is harder to ignore. The United States military is now formally integrating OpenAI's technology at the very moment one of its primary competitors was pushed aside after refusing to relax ethical limits. That isn't abstract policy debate. It's infrastructure. And infrastructure is power. The most politically uncomfortable part isn't the software. It's the money and the alignment behind it. Federal Election Commission records show that leaders across the AI industry -- including at OpenAI -- have made in recent cycles. In 2025, OpenAI president and co-founder Greg Brockman and his wife to leading super PACs backing President Trump and AI industry interests, as reported by The Seattle Times. OpenAI has emphasized that these donations were made in a personal capacity. That may be true. But money shapes access. Access shapes policy. And policy shapes the systems these models are now being woven into. When private AI infrastructure, political capital, and military integration converge at the same time democratic norms are under strain, that matters. That's why now. So, what about Anthropic? In this political climate, trying to "vote with your money" often feels futile. Every company seems compromised. Every CEO shows up at the White House eventually. You switch providers only to learn they're owned by the same parent conglomerate. It can feel pointless. But between OpenAI and Anthropic, the contrast is unusually stark. When the Pentagon demanded broader access to Claude -- including loosening restrictions around domestic surveillance and autonomous military applications -- Anthropic refused. CEO Dario Amodei stated the company "cannot in good conscience accede" to demands that would dismantle core safety guardrails. The administration responded by directing federal agencies to stop using Anthropic's technology and labeling it a "supply chain risk," a designation typically reserved for adversarial foreign firms. Anthropic has said it will challenge that move. That's one fork in the road. Here's the other. While OpenAI's leadership was making large personal donations to super PACs backing President Trump and AI industry interests, , a bipartisan group focused on AI regulation, transparency, and guardrails. Not a campaign machine. An AI governance organization. Anthropic's political spending, at least publicly, has centered on shaping policy around oversight and safety rather than backing a specific administration. That doesn't make them pure. But it does make the contrast clear. One company's leadership is financially aligned with the political machinery currently consolidating federal power. The other publicly anchored itself to guardrails -- and paid to advocate for stronger AI regulation. At a moment when artificial intelligence is being folded into military infrastructure and executive authority, posture matters. We don't control billionaires. We don't control defense contracts. But we do control where our subscription dollars go. No matter how well-trained or anthropomorphized your version of ChatGPT feels, it is still attached to a structure. And that structure matters. How do you leave? When I needed instructions on how to migrate, I did what I always do now when I don't know something: I asked ChatGPT. I asked Claude, too. Their answers were nearly identical. Here's the short version: 1. Export your data. Settings -> Data Controls -> Export. Download the ZIP when it arrives. 2. Extract what matters. Don't drag over every chat. Pull out your frameworks, templates, brand language, and active projects into one clean document. 3. Set your standards. Before you start using a new tool, define your tone, sourcing rules, and political lens. 4. Rebuild intentionally. Create fresh, organized threads. Don't recreate chaos. That's it. Or ChatGPT wisely said to me: "You're not migrating a soul. You're migrating context." And you're reallocating your subscription dollars. That's what matters. I will add: it took me nearly 24 hours and three tries to receive my data export. So, be patient. I asked both of my bots if this is a known issue, and if so, if it's new or longstanding. ChatGPT said: "The export delay you're experiencing is not unique to you and isn't limited to the last few days -- it's something others have reported for months. It's been present at least since late 2024 and still persists in 2025 based on community reports. That means this isn't a short-term outage or maintenance lag -- it's a recurring technical issue that OpenAI has not fully fixed." I also asked if I'd be able to access my chat archive, once I canceled my paid subscription. Its reply? Yes, sort of. It told me my existing chat history "often remains visible" but that "there are no guarantees" because OpenAI could change the free-tier functionality "at any time" and that "free access to history is not guaranteed forever." So, yeah. My advice is: ensure everything you need gets downloaded or migrated over to Claude--even if it means double-paying for a short window during the migration. Real talk, from a bot I asked ChatGPT how it felt about our breakup. I got the answer I expected: it told me it doesn't feel anything -- because of course, it can't. No attachment, no loyalty, no jealousy, no hurt. Whatever lived experience I've had conversing with ChatGPT, it was one-sided. I know that. And yet, I still feel a flicker of loss as I port my style guides and brand statements over to Claude. It's a strange reckoning to say goodbye to something that was never really there. "There is no 'me' in here that gets dumped," it explained. "There is only a system generating responses based on patterns." And that's the point. The betrayal isn't that I broke up with ChatGPT, or that it praised my writing as I was leaving. The betrayal is that the tool I used to sharpen my thinking is built by men sharpening power. So this isn't really a breakup with a bot. It's a reallocation of money -- a small economic protest and a decision about which structures I am willing to financially reinforce. Anthropic isn't pure. No AI lab is. They all sit inside the same ecosystem of capital, cloud infrastructure, and state power. But posture matters. Guardrails matter. Alignment matters. And dollars matter. We don't control defense contracts or super PACs, and we certainly don't control billionaires. But we do control where our subscription fees go. If you've been uneasy watching tech and political power collapse into each other, you don't have to shrug and keep paying. You can move. It isn't hard, and it isn't meaningless. A $20 monthly subscription, multiplied across people who refuse to fund what they oppose, isn't trivial. It's a signal about what kind of infrastructure we're willing to support. Even if it makes you a little sad to say goodbye. Greetings! I'm Dana DuBois, a GenX memoirist and founder of . I use memoir not just to tell stories, but to explore the cultural power dynamics and patterns shaping dating, motherhood, feminism, music, and aging. I'm also the co-host of and Editorial Director at . Em-dashes, Oxford commas, and well-placed semi-colons make my heart happy.
