I’m running to be Colorado’s next governor — because I truly believe our state deserves a fighter. = | | = | = I came to Colorado for a job interview over three decades ago, and right away I was hooked. I love how innovative and independent Coloradans are. I love how we care about one another. And I love how we cherish our natural resources, are proud of our beautiful state, and protect our land, air, and water. I am honored by the opportunity to fight for you, serving as your attorney general for the past several years. My wife and I have called Colorado home for many years, and we plan to live here for many more. But, I worry about whether our two kids — both of whom grew up here — will be able to do the same. After touring our state more than once to have conversations with you, one of the top concerns I’ve heard is whether people can afford to live in Colorado. From health care to housing to child care and beyond, Coloradans everywhere are getting squeezed. They want their next governor to fight for them and forge solutions that can help more of us stay in the state we love. I decided to run for governor because I am ready to meet these challenges head-on and lead our state on day one. You’ve also told me about how much you want your next governor to fight back against the Trump administration’s disrespect for our rights and the rule of law. This week, Kristi Noem sat before Congress. And so did four families whose loved ones were taken from them. Peter, I was in the room when Kristi Noem sat before the Senate Judiciary Committee... and I watched as she had to face the families whose lives her policies have torn apart. [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvd8hCserj-XmGYLB0-0IMX1om1J0_1aEV2b-kAgyJHHnBxpDS5WqXdGhM0caZ_h88AY3rJ00-MOnpSMrGIaSW6wryMqo_CIkQpmYnPvhEzO_WhRxCQe-png7SgvhVx2USz_XKVNWEzL4SeFk1d4BtAejGkwrcnTZq2m-DP4Zfjg1_L2KShVHUPPf-tBdwh2p3LCKiAmDcBsrzBMwJJl_wk9quX38c9bVqveoK2uTY5JqpbwbmGbg42Q6JUuusLSBmwQdg7rfx3RSjiY4cCawMcUu5EAdN9ezLUNG1ZQ69JcE0-jpFi8pG1Aqf-HLRKptYl13kFqO_Wg9OGVPBbXdYqlDkjm1BGXcmfVS047typPjGPHyr3G9nC2BwKQ3Ri7_3CNfMTfw6Bo14fz3xi2iokpZv396glwWcUh5v6WPYg5A/4on/Y5HNobivQDmp8-sEPcKqjg/h0/h001.igzBBSu4YM_P-M2kB9RCZP6Zat8HaqtQXmMGWxZOEKk) [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvd8hCserj-XmGYLB0-0IMX1om1J0_1aEV2b-kAgyJHHnBxpDS5WqXdGhM0caZ_h88AY3rJ00-MOnpSMrGIaSW66oPP4acDTl2eJWKzIoK-ac4Dm6QZD_ull3qMt68VDSFTWYKzi2Qbm0r5DOozBIwrWQ_KNEPYZFfCe45fLl_AQxat9jrBDVa9Ho8DOa7q9oYkR1OA_A-TBHMIrEq_ubsEUjDMsKEOmEQ6_UPNWx-S3a1Mdgl9yhhCP_M9EWhOHBeDTUAgDHYi3MK24a2nDgI1FQrRIqxgc6BqJ26TfkElGHzef7ZSFKsYN-6U0LoSE4M0i98fzlWkHbmdSZw3T_ikrUnTIR2qrHujB0qNThA8VFyK224yQaQDHzM0vno49er7wI_061_tpz8zVtwucsOHRvlOh-0Io7yBsSNQc-k4rQ/4on/Y5HNobivQDmp8-sEPcKqjg/h1/h001.ppK3eBxJ9RcGuUjxJnpXwYVATNhcVB5jCHKs6RT0b6g) **The Workers Circle flew these four families to Washington, DC to testify before Congress.** These are families with loved ones who have been in ICE detention camps **at Alligator Alcatraz, Krome Detention Center in Miami, and Stewart Detention Center in Georgia**. I spent the last several days working with Congressional staff to make sure they had a seat at the table. And they used it in a way I could barely believe – putting human faces and real stories against the sterile statistics that the Department of Homeland Security loves to hide behind. **These families missed days of work and lost wages they couldn't afford to lose to be here to speak on behalf of their loved ones.** That’s how important this fight is. clean_body: | | This week, Kristi Noem sat before Congress. And so did four families whose loved ones were taken from them. Peter, I was in the room when Kristi Noem sat before the Senate Judiciary Committee... and I watched as she had to face the families whose lives her policies have torn apart. The Workers Circle flew these four families to Washington, DC to testify before Congress. These are families with loved ones who have been in ICE detention camps at Alligator Alcatraz, Krome Detention Center in Miami, and Stewart Detention Center in Georgia. I spent the last several days working with Congressional staff to make sure they had a seat at the table. And they used it in a way I could barely believe – putting human faces and real stories against the sterile statistics that the Department of Homeland Security loves to hide behind. These families missed days of work and lost wages they couldn't afford to lose to be here to speak on behalf of their loved ones. That’s how important this fight is. This could not have happened without the generous support of people just like you and groups like United for Democracy refusing to accept the inhumanity that this administration parades each and every day, demanding that we accept it.We need to raise $10,000 to cover the full expenses of this critical trip, for 9 people****which includes last minute (expensive) airfare, hotel, and meals. I've spent my career fighting for social justice, and I can tell you: this is how change happens. Not just through lawsuits and legislation – though those matter too. Change happens when the people making decisions can no longer pretend the consequences are abstract. When a daughter who hasn't seen her father in months is in the same room as the person who authorized his detention,the wall between policy and humanity gets thinner. Let me level with you, Peter. body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]
Friends, I just spoke on the House floor ahead of tomorrow’s vote on a war powers resolution to stop Donald Trump from continuing illegal military operations in Iran without congressional authorization.
I want to share some of what I said with you.
In Congress I strive to be a voice for my generation. I’m also incredibly proud to represent our military community in San Diego — the largest military community in the country. And in both of those roles, I cannot stay quiet in this critical moment.
When presidents from both sides of the aisle have taken military action, it is our service members and young people from San Diego who are sent into harm’s way.
They sacrifice their bodies, their mental health, their time with loved ones, and even their lives — for us.
And while they’re willing to make those sacrifices, we in Congress should be damn sure it’s worth it.
Too often, it’s not.
Too often, wars last longer and cost more than promised.
Too often, regime change plans go awry — like we’ve already seen with the deaths of 6 service members and hundreds of civilians.
My colleagues claim voting for this war powers resolution hurts service members.
The opposite is true.
We owe our service members a real debate before we send them into harm’s way. Voting yes on this war powers resolution is a vote FOR our military — to ensure their sacrifices won't be in vain.
And to any of my colleagues who vote no: I ask you to come to my district, look our service members in the eye, and explain why you believe debating and voting before we risk their lives is a bad thing.
We know that my Republican colleagues in the House could very well vote this legislation down.
That’s shameful. So now is the time to take action. There are three key things to do right now: [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]
1. Call the Capitol switchboard at (202) 224-3121. Speak to every Republican Member of Congress’s office you possibly can, and urge them in the strongest possible terms to vote yes. When you’re done, ask all your friends and family to do the same.

2. Share information about this online and in conversation with your networks. Talking about these issues is a really important part of building the support we need to push back.

3. When you can, donate to the Democratic House candidates who need your support — especially those who vote the right way on this critical legislation despite pressure to do otherwise. I’m not asking you for money today, but we will need all hands on deck to flip the House in November and I hope you’ll be a part of that work however you’re able. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]
Thank you for stepping up and being such a meaningful part of this work when it matters most.
More soon,
Sara [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]

| **New Poll: 79% of Mississippi Voters Support Term Limits on Congress**
---
| A new poll of registered voters in Mississippi reveals a massive groundswell of support for term limits on members of Congress. The poll, conducted by RMG Research between January 5-8, 2026, shows that 79% of Mississippi voters approve of placing term limits on Congress. This sentiment transcends party lines, including 87% of Republicans, 65% of Democrats, and 62% of Independents. “These results send a clear and unmistakable message to Mississippi,” says USTL President, Philip Blumel. “Mississippi voters are tired of career politicians in Washington and are looking to their state legislators to take the lead on this critical reform.”
---

### **_Stand for Health Freedom endorses Ron Eller for Congress_****.**
Stand for Health Freedom has endorsed conservative Republican Ron Eller for the Second Congressional District of Mississippi. With the Republican primary just days away on March 10, Eller is again receiving the support of conservative activists nationwide against his primary opponent.

Eller, a Physician’s Assistant in Jackson, expressed his gratitude for the endorsement: “It is my great honor to receive Stand for Health Freedom's endorsement. I have long respected this highly effective advocacy organization for its stalwart defender of individual liberty and health freedom.”

Like Stand for Health Freedom, Eller has consistently advocated individual freedom of choice and opposed vaccine and mask mandates and centralized government control over health care. Eller stated, “Stand for Health Freedom supports candidates who make and support policy to protect and expand individual and family choice in matters of personal health. I will defend and expand these rights for Mississippi residents.”

Leah Wilson, Executive Director of Stand for Health Freedom, says, “We are seeing an increasing number of medical professionals and physicians prioritize health freedom. They see the value in protecting each individual in order to have a community of healthy and free individuals. Eller is a shining example and will represent Mississippi with the backbone and principles that are needed to fix what’s broken in Washington.”

Stand for Health Freedom (SHF) endorses political candidates who prioritize individual liberty, medical freedom, and informed consent. These endorsements highlight a commitment to reducing government overreach in personal healthcare decisions. Key themes of endorsed candidates often include:

**Medical Freedom:** Protecting the right to make personal health decisions without government mandates.

**Informed Consent:** Ensuring transparency and personal choice in medical treatments.

**Legislative Action:** Opposing government overreach and defending constitutional rights.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: I am the Democratic nominee for Governor of Texas
body:
Texans are ready for a governor who works for them.
#
We did it!
**Because of your support, we cleared the first hurdle, and I will officially be facing Greg Abbott this November in the race for Governor of Texas.**
Now the real work begins. Over the next eight months, my team and I will travel across Texas to share our message, talk with voters about what is at stake, and build the kind of campaign that can win. That means scaling up our field program, hiring staff, and getting our message on TV and online so Texans hear the truth, not Abbott’s lies.
And if there’s anything this primary election showed us, it’s that Texans are already showing up. More Democrats voted than Republicans during the first week of early voting in the primary, and turnout was higher than it has been in years.
Texans are paying attention, and they’re ready for a governor with integrity who works for them, not against them.
But we can’t take anything for granted. To win in November, we have to turn that energy into a statewide movement, starting right now.
**[So I am asking: can you help us kick off this race on the right foot by becoming a General Election Founding Donor and pitching in to my campaign today?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21583?c0=leftnet_em20260304_partner_ms_gh_em_leftnet.PeLAGq&refcode=em20260304-1520&t=1&akid=1520%2E2118727%2E-KGYf2)**
